explain: This is a fundamental resection problem specific to plane table surveying.

q: 2. The size of plane table is
explain: Standard surveying plane tables typically measure 600mm by 750mm.

q: 3. The process of aligning the plane table by rotating it in the horizontal plane to the corresponding lines on the ground
explain: Rotation to align with ground features is the definition of orientation.

q: 4. The triangle formed by joining the position of the known points on plane table survey is known as
explain: In the context of the three-point problem, the triangle formed by the three known points is called the great triangle.

q: 5. In case of resection method of plane table, the relation between great triangle and great circle are
options: the area of great triangle is more than great circle
the area of great triangle is less than great circle
the area of great triangle is equal to great circle
explain: Geometrically, the circle passing through the three points (great circle) encloses the triangle (great triangle).

q: 6. Three-point problem can be solved by
explain: The three-point problem for orienting a plane table can be solved by several standard techniques, including the tracing paper method, Bessel's (mechanical/graphical) method, and Lehmann's method, so all are valid solutions.

q: 7. Strength of fix of a plane table is
options: accuracy in locating the position of instrument station by taking observation to three stations
fixity of table while solving two point problem
explain: Strength of fix refers to how accurately the table's position is determined relative to the known points.

q: 8. The fix of table is good when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the middle station is much nearer than other two stations
the angle subtended between two stations is not very small
explain: A good fix requires geometry that avoids 'danger circles' where the position becomes indeterminate.

q: 9. A poor fix of the table is
options: when station is within the great triangle
when station is near the great circle
explain: If the instrument station lies on or near the circle passing through the three known points, the solution becomes unreliable.

q: 10. The strength of fix' is poor when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the station is outside the great circle
the station is on the great circle
the station is within the great circle but outside the great triangle
explain: The position is indeterminate if the station is on the circumference of the great circle. [2] the station is within the great circle but outside the great triangle become the 2nd bestnchoice

q: 11. The two point problem and three point problems are methods of
explain: Both problems solve for the station's location and the table's orientation simultaneously.

q: 12. The resection by two point problem as compared to the three point problem
explain: Two-point resection is more cumbersome and usually less accurate than three-point resection.

q: 13. If the plane table is not horizontal in a direction at right angles to the alidade, the line of sight is parallel to fiducial edge only for
explain: Errors due to non-horizontality are minimized or eliminated when the line of sight itself is horizontal.

q: 14. To orient a plane table without two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted is
explain: The two-point problem is the specific procedure used to orient when only two points are available and distance measurement is not possible.

q: 15. Which one of the following is not a personal error ?
options: the table not being perfectly leveled
the table not being perfectly central
the table not being perfectly clamped
explain: All listed items (levelling, centering, clamping) are under the surveyor's control and are therefore personal/instrumental setup errors.

q: 16. The method of plane tabling in which plane table is set only one station to take detail is known as
explain: Radiation involves taking rays and distances to all points from a single setup.

q: 17. Detailed plotting is generally done by
explain: Radiation is the most efficient way to plot numerous nearby details once the station is established.

q: 18. Radiation method of plane table survey is the best suited when
explain: Since distances must be measured (usually with a tape/chain), it is best for short, clear paths.

q: 19. In plane table instrument for horizontal & vertical measurement without chaining
explain: A telescopic alidade is equipped with stadia hairs for distance and a vertical circle for slope angles.

q: 20. The method most suitable for plotting in hilly areas is
explain: Intersection is preferred in hills where measuring horizontal distance on steep slopes is difficult.

q: 21. Actually which is not the method of plane tabling ?
explain: Per the provided key, 'resection' is listed as the 'not' method here, likely referring to its role as a location tool rather than a detail plotting tool in this specific context.

q: 22. The instrument used for centering the plane table accurately is
explain: The plumbing fork (or U-frame) carries a plumb bob to transfer the ground point to the paper.

q: 23. The orientation of the table is done by
explain: The table can be oriented using a compass (magnetic needle) or by aligning a line with a previously occupied station (back sighting).

q: 24. "Fiducial edge " is the working edge of
explain: The bevelled ruler edge of the alidade used for drawing rays is the fiducial edge.

q: 25. Which instrument is not used in plane table ?
explain: An altimeter is used for measuring altitude via pressure, not standard plane table plotting.

q: 26. The size of plane table is .............
explain: While various sizes exist, the standard size for a large plane table used in professional surveying is typically 600 mm x 750 mm.

q: 27. The technique of plotting all the accessible stations with a single set up of plane table is called
explain: As stated in Q104, this technique of plotting all accessible points from a single plane table setup is called radiation.

q: 28. In case of telescopic alidade, the adjustment done is
options: the line of collimation should perpendicular to the axis of telescope
the horizontal axis should be parallel to the alidade rule
the bubble line of telescope level should be parallel to the plane of collimation
explain: Telescopic alidades require these permanent adjustments to ensure the line of sight accurately reflects the horizontal and vertical positions plotted on the sheet.

q: 29. An instrument resembling an alidade is
explain: A tangent clinometer (or Indian clinometer) consists of two vanes similar to an alidade and is used on a plane table to determine the heights of objects.

q: 30. Usefulness of plane table is enhanced by providing
explain: The Indian tangent clinometer allows the plane table surveyor to determine the heights of points and ground slopes effectively.

q: 31. For the revision of an existing survey with the help of plane table we generally use
explain: Resection is used to establish the current position of the plane table on the map by sighting back to points already plotted.

q: 32. A point determined by resection on a plane table is called
explain: A 'fix' is the location of the plane table instrument station on the drawing sheet determined through the resection process.

q: 33. The instrument which is used in plane tabling for obtaining horizontal and vertical distance directly without resorting to chaining, is known as
explain: A telescopic alidade is equipped with stadia hairs, allowing the surveyor to compute distances and elevations optically rather than using a tape or chain.

q: 34. The operation of revolving a plane table about its vertical axis so that all lines on the sheet become parallel to corresponding lines on the ground, is known
explain: Orientation ensures that the map is correctly aligned with the cardinal directions on the ground, making all lines on the paper parallel to their ground counterparts.

q: 35. In setting up a plane table at any station
options: both leveling and centering are done simultaneously
explain: In modern practice, leveling and centering are performed at the same time to ensure the board is horizontal and the point is accurately represented above the ground station.

q: 36. A disadvantage of plane table survey is
options: cannot be used in wet climate
details not available while redrawing to different scale
explain: Since the map is plotted directly in the field on a specific scale, it is difficult to reproduce the survey accurately if a change in scale is required later in the office.

q: 37. Detailed plotting is generally done by
explain: Radiation, intersection, and traversing are all primary methods used in plane table surveying to plot the details of a map.

q: 38. The type of surveying which requires least office work is
explain: Since the map is drawn directly in the field, plane table surveying eliminates the need for extensive office calculations and plotting.

q: 39. Intersection method of detailed plotting is most suitable for
explain: Intersection is ideal for hilly or broken ground where measuring distances with a chain or tape is difficult or impossible.

q: 40. The plane table surveying is
explain: Plane tabling is efficient for small scales, isn't affected by magnetic interference (unlike a compass), and generally requires less expensive equipment.

q: 41. The operation of turning the table so all lines are parallel to corresponding ground lines is
explain: Orientation is the process of keeping the table at each successive station parallel to its position at the first station.

q: 42. The plotting of small areas commanded from a single station is usually done by
explain: Radiation is the simplest method where points are plotted by drawing rays from a single instrument station and measuring distances along those rays.

q: 43. The method of intersection in plane tabling is commonly used for
explain: Intersection allows the surveyor to plot points (like a church spire or a peak) that cannot be reached or chained easily.

q: 44. The method of plane tabling commonly used for establishing instrument stations only is
explain: Resection is primarily used to determine the location of the instrument station itself on the map using previously plotted points.

q: 45. If the plane table is not horizontal in a direction at right angles to the alidade, the line of sight is parallel to the fiducial edge only for .............
explain: If the table is tilted, the line of sight and the fiducial edge are only parallel when looking horizontally; any vertical angle will introduce a lateral error.

q: 46. The method of surveying in which field work and plotting work are done simultaneously, is called .............
explain: Plane table surveying is unique because the map is drawn in the field while observations are being made.

q: 47. The two point problem and three point problem are methods of .............
explain: These methods allow a surveyor to locate the table's position (resection) and align the table (orientation) simultaneously using known points.

q: 48. In plate tabling, the instrument used to measure horizontal and vertical distance directly is known as .............
explain: A telescopic alidade is equipped with a telescope and stadia hairs, allowing the surveyor to determine distances and elevations without manual chaining.

q: 49. Which of the following methods of plane table surveying is used to locate the position of an inaccessible points?
explain: Intersection is the method where a point is located by the intersection of two rays from two different stations, making it ideal for points that cannot be reached.

q: 50. The resection by two point problem as compared to three point problem .............
explain: The two-point problem is more involved and requires an auxiliary station and more sightings, making it more laborious than the three-point problem.
